name: Short-duration crypto up/down: spot-lead / oracle-aware latency taking

seed_category: new (latency trading of short-duration crypto markets)
one_line: Hit stale up/down quotes after Binance/Chainlink moves; the poster-child strategy of 2025 that public millisecond data now shows negative after fees for non-HFT takers.
scope: Cover the taker side: history (0x8dxd-style wallets, fee introduction Jan-Mar 2026, 250 ms then 50 ms delay, TWAP settlement), the measured lag (347 ms median response, 16 ms median lead-lag), the fee at mid prices (up to 1.75c/share) and how taker-rebate tier changes break-even, Binance-vs-Chainlink basis, and the body of null and loss results (OpenMarket -0.116/trade, pre-registered btc-edge study, uruguabot, last-60-second entries -37.81%, paper-vs-live gaps). State clearly what infrastructure would be needed and whether the Aug 2026 delay cut reopens anything. Boundary: maker side is short-crypto-maker-side; spot pushing at expiry is oracle-input-manipulation; buying 95c+ decided windows is near-certain-bond-carry; TWAP partial-average pricing is speculative band.

critic_notes: short-crypto-latency-taker: maturity 'Established' contradicts its own scope (negative after fees for non-HFT takers; OpenMarket -0.116 per trade; pre-registered null). The Oracle (2026-04-24, fetched) confirms the poster-child crypto bot has been inactive since March 2026, and E4's reconstruction says 94% of that wallet's trades were paired YES+NO buys, not spot-lag snipes. Label it 'Established historically, decayed: no evidence of current profitability'. Category 'Arbitrage' is also wrong: it is directional latency taking with fee and adverse-selection risk.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Short-dated crypto: spot-lead / oracle-aware taker
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Buy the side implied by a Binance/Chainlink move before the Polymarket book reprices, tracking the actual Chainlink (now TWAP) settlement source.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Watch spot (Binance) and the Chainlink Data Streams feed that actually settles the market; when spot moves beyond a threshold relative to the window's reference price, take the corresponding Up/Down token if still cheap. Practitioners report Binance-vs-Chainlink divergences of 0.3-0.8% for 10-30 s in volatile moments, so watching the wrong feed flips close trades. Since 2026-08-07 settlement is a Chainlink TWAP (60 s for 5m since 2026-08-14), so the target is the expected average, not the last print.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Claimed 30-90 s repricing lag of Polymarket vs spot; oracle-basis awareness.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Evidence is contradictory: small samples show 70-80% win rates; the largest retail dataset found the ask already prices it (momentum side resolved 74.8% while Poly asked 75.3%).
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Fees (up to 1.75/100 shares at 50c) exceed the edge; paper-vs-live gap (+11% simulated vs -27% live; stops overshoot 86% of the time); positions API lag creating ghost positions; non-stationary 5-minute regimes (ML 57% train -> 48-50% live); losses documented: -$270 (uruguabot), -37.81% (supermalvo last-60s entries), 23-trade sample +$11.51 only.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Use the public OpenMarket-style synchronized Polymarket-Binance data or your own recorder; test fillable asks (not mids) 1-5 s after threshold moves, net of the 0.07 fee curve, over >=200 windows.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: CEX-to-Polymarket latency arbitrage on crypto up/down contracts
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Hit stale Polymarket quotes after Binance/Chainlink moves; public millisecond data says the edge is negative after fees for anyone not at the very front of the queue.
raw_discovery_candidates.maturity: Emerging (research evidence is negative for non-colocated takers)
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Derive a fair digital price from spot (log-normal or empirical model), compare with the Polymarket book, and take liquidity when the quote is stale. The documented venue response lag to a >=5 bp Binance move is a median 347 ms, against a 16 ms median timestamp lead-lag. Takers face the platform taker delay (250 ms until 2026-08-17, 50 ms since) and the peak of the fee curve, since these contracts sit near p=0.5.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Speed versus makers who reprice slowly.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: It mostly does not: spreads are one tick 91.9% of the time and the fee at p=0.5 is ~1.75 c/share (derived from rate 0.07). The 50 ms delay change in Aug-2026 shifts advantage from makers to fast takers, which is the one reason to re-test.

evidence.title: OpenMarket: A Synchronized Polymarket-Binance Dataset for High-Frequency Prediction-Market Research (Young), arXiv
evidence.supports: 727,098,247 rows, 2.94M lead-lag pairs, Feb-12..May-15-2026: median lag 16 ms (5th/95th -186/+316 ms); median response to large Binance moves 347 ms; walk-forward model AUC 0.8377 vs 0.8405 for the Polymarket mid itself; simulated trading -0.116 normalised payoff per trade at 1% fee + 0.5% slippage.

evidence.title: Polymarket changelog
evidence.supports: Taker delay on crypto markets 250 ms -> 50 ms (2026-08-17); 5-min markets launched 2026-02-12 with taker fees; fees extended to all crypto durations 2026-03-06; Chainlink TWAP resolution 2026-08-07/14.

evidence.title: PolySwarm: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Prediction Market Trading and Latency Arbitrage (Barot, Borkhatariya), arXiv
evidence.supports: Describes a CEX-implied-probability latency module with quarter-Kelly sizing but reports no live or backtest PnL - architecture only.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Negative expectancy after fees in the only public ms-level study; adverse selection by faster takers; you pay the fee that funds makers' rebates; REST polling (5 s) is two orders of magnitude too slow.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Re-run OpenMarket-style measurement on post-2026-08-17 data (50 ms delay, TWAP settlement): distribution of stale-quote size x duration net of the 0.07 fee curve. If median capturable edge < fee, drop it.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Spot-lag latency taking on crypto up/down markets (5m/15m/1h)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Hit stale Polymarket up/down quotes when Binance/Coinbase spot has already moved, before makers reprice.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Bot streams exchange spot/order-flow and the Polymarket book for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP up/down contracts. When spot moves enough that the true probability is e.g. ~85% while the book still shows ~50/50, it takes the stale side and holds to the 5/15-minute resolution. Since 2026 the trade pays a taker fee of 0.07*p*(1-p) per share (peak $1.75 per 100 shares), passes a 50 ms taker delay (250 ms before 2026-08-17) and settles on a 60 s Chainlink TWAP rather than a snapshot. Profitability now depends on sub-100 ms infrastructure plus a high Taker Rebate tier.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Speed: Polymarket quotes respond to large Binance moves after a median 347 ms (collector-clock event study); retail-heavy counterparties.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: The lag is measured and real, and flow in these markets is retail-dominated. But it is the most contested niche on the venue and Polymarket has explicitly priced it (fees, delay, TWAP).

evidence.title: Arbitrage Bots Dominate Polymarket With Millions in Profits as Humans Fall Behind (BeInCrypto via Yahoo Finance)
evidence.supports: Wallet analysis: bot exploiting lag vs Binance/Coinbase on BTC/ETH/SOL 15-min markets, $313 -> $414,000 in one month, 98% win rate, $4-5k per trade. Secondary report of an X wallet analysis; not independently verified.

evidence.title: OpenMarket: A Synchronized Polymarket-Binance Dataset (G. Young, arXiv)
evidence.supports: 727M rows, 54 days (2026-02-12..05-15); median 347 ms Polymarket response to large Binance moves; 43-feature walk-forward model does NOT beat the book, -0.116 payoff units per trade after fees/slippage. Hard negative result for non-HFT entrants.

evidence.title: Polymarket quietly introduces taker fees on 15-minute crypto markets (Cointelegraph)
evidence.supports: Fees introduced specifically on these markets, described by traders as directed against high-frequency bots; proceeds rebated to makers.

evidence.title: Polymarket changelog (official docs)
evidence.supports: Crypto taker delay now 50 ms, down from 250 ms; TWAP resolution since 2026-08-07; crypto fee expansion dates.

evidence.title: Ask HN: Anyone trading prediction markets programmatically?
evidence.supports: Practitioner tried 5m/15m crypto arb and found it 'way too competitive and HFT' for an individual.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Fee at 50c eats 3.5% of premium; taker delay lets makers cancel; TWAP settlement breaks naive last-tick payoff models; one public attempt with ms-level data found no out-of-sample edge; small bots lose (uruguabot: -$270 over 4,000+ logged trades, stop-loss slippage mean -6c).
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Replay the public OpenMarket corpus: trigger on Binance moves > X bp, fill at Polymarket book 50 ms later, subtract 0.07*p*(1-p); require positive markout before writing any execution code.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Spot-led latency arbitrage on crypto up/down markets (Binance or Chainlink into Polymarket)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: The most-copied 'bot strategy' of 2025. For a retail-grade stack it is now demonstrably negative after fees, the delay and TWAP settlement.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Watch Binance order flow and the Chainlink stream. When spot moves, hit stale 5-minute, 15-minute or hourly up/down quotes before makers re-price. Polymarket responded in stages: taker fees from 2026-01-05, now a 0.07 rate on all crypto markets; a taker delay; and TWAP resolution. The Polymarket quote response to large Binance moves is a median 347 ms. A taker therefore has to clear the fee, roughly 1.75c per share at 50c, plus the delay window in which makers can pull their quotes.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Pure speed against slow makers. It was historically large and is now fee-gated.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: For a small team as a taker it mostly does not. The honest reason to include it is that two public, careful null results exist. The winning variant is the maker side, covered in the speed-bump candidate.

evidence.title: OpenMarket: A Synchronized Polymarket-Binance Dataset
evidence.supports: 727M rows from Feb-May 2026. A 43-feature walk-forward model does not beat Polymarket's own implied probability. Simulated trading nets -0.116 payoff units per trade after fees and slippage. The median lag is 16 ms, and the quote response to large Binance moves is a median 347 ms.

evidence.title: polymarket-btc-edge, a pre-registered study
evidence.supports: 9,225 windows, 11 Bonferroni-corrected hypotheses on Deribit order-flow signals: 'No edge for taker after realistic costs.' An earlier 54% momentum finding was publicly retracted for lookahead bias.

evidence.title: Polymarket changelog
evidence.supports: Taker fees on 15-minute crypto markets from Jan 5, 2026 (peak 1.56%). 5-minute markets launched Feb 12. All crypto markets carry fees from Mar 1. Delay cut from 250 ms to 50 ms on Aug 17.

evidence.title: How Latency Impacts Polymarket Bot Performance
evidence.supports: Anecdote: a bot on the BTC 15-minute market went $1,000 to $1,869 in days, then lost 50% in two days after a parameter change. This is typical of overfit results.

evidence.title: Lag Arbitrage Shows Prediction Markets Are Now a Speed Game
evidence.supports: Claims a bot made $385k trading the BTC probability lag. The claim is unsourced.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Fees exceed the edge, makers cancel inside the delay, TWAP settlement removes last-second certainty, and the space is crowded with GitHub bots carrying over 1,000 stars.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Do not rebuild it. Download OpenMarket or marketlens data, apply the current 0.07 fee and 50 ms delay, and replicate the null result in a day.
